body.en: Algebra 2 is really the study of functions as objects you can combine, invert and transform. Fluency with notation, domain and range underpins every later chapter.
A function assigns to each input exactly one output. We write \( y=f(x) \); the set of allowed inputs is the domain and the set of resulting outputs is the range.

body.en:
Given \( f(x)=2x+1 \) and \( g(x)=x^{2} \), find \( f\big(g(2)\big) \).

Work inside-out: \( g(2)=4 \), then \( f(4)=2(4)+1 \):

\[ f\big(g(2)\big)=9. \]

Find the inverse of \( f(x)=2x-6 \).

Write \( y=2x-6 \), swap and solve: \( x=2y-6 \Rightarrow y=\tfrac{x+6}{2} \):

\[ f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+6}{2}. \]

body.en:
• Horizontal Shift Intuition: In \(f(x - h)\), subtracting \(h\) shifts the graph to the right by \(h\), while \(f(x + h)\) shifts to the left. Vertical shifts \(f(x) \pm k\) behave normally (\(+k\) is up, \(-k\) is down).
  • Composition Order: \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) evaluates \(g(x)\) first, then applies \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\). Do not multiply functions when composition is requested!
  • Inverse Domain/Range Swap: For an invertible function \(f\), the domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\), and the range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\). If the original function is restricted (e.g. \(x \ge 0\)), that restriction dictates the range of \(f^{-1}\).
  • Even vs. Odd Functions: \(f\) is even if \(f(-x) = f(x)\) (symmetric across the \(y\)-axis, e.g. \(x^2, \cos x\)); \(f\) is odd if \(f(-x) = -f(x)\) (symmetric about the origin, e.g. \(x^3, \sin x\)).

label.en: Worked Example C — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 4)(x - 9) = 0 \implies x = 4 \text{ or } x = 9 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 4 + 9 = \mathbf{13} \) and product \( = (4)(9) = \mathbf{36} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

question.en: If \(f(x)=x^2-1\) and \(g(x)=\sqrt{x+2}\), find (a) \(f(g(3))\), (b) the domain of \(g\circ f\).
Find the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) and state its domain and range for \(f(x) = \dfrac{3x - 1}{2x + 5}\).

solution.en:
Write \(y = \dfrac{3x - 1}{2x + 5}\). The domain of \(f\) is \(x eq -2.5\). Its horizontal asymptote is \(y = 3/2\), so the range of \(f\) is \(y eq 1.5\).

Swap \(x\) and \(y\) and solve for \(y\):

\[x = rac{3y - 1}{2y + 5} \implies x(2y + 5) = 3y - 1.\]\[2xy + 5x = 3y - 1 \implies 2xy - 3y = -5x - 1.\]\[y(2x - 3) = -(5x + 1) \implies y = rac{-5x - 1}{2x - 3} = rac{5x + 1}{3 - 2x}.\]

Inverse function: \[f^{-1}(x) = rac{5x + 1}{3 - 2x}.\]

Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \(x eq rac{3}{2}\) (the range of \(f\)).

Range of \(f^{-1}\): \(y eq - rac{5}{2}\) (the domain of \(f\)).

question.en: [Functions & Their Graphs · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Functions & Their Graphs · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
